# FDG9063

> CONSIDER implementing the Basic Dispose Pattern on classes that themselves don’t hold unmanaged resources or disposable objects, but are likely to have subtypes that do.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.4 Dispose Pattern.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library suggestion, application none, test none
- Status: verified

Library only: the reason given is subtypes that hold resources, which users of the framework write by deriving from the class (System.IO.Stream). Not machine-checkable: whether subtypes are likely to hold unmanaged resources or disposable objects is a design judgment.

## From the book

A great example of this is the `System.IO.Stream` class. Although it is an abstract base class that doesn’t hold any resources, most of its subclasses do—and because of this, it implements this pattern.
